# Phase 1 — stand up the host-operations abstraction

*Companion to [`plan.md`](./plan.md) and
[`phase0-cpp-classification.md`](./phase0-cpp-classification.md). Deliverable for
**Phase 1**: introduce the host abstraction with no behaviour change. Call sites
are still unconverted — that is Phase 2.*

## Naming reconciliation with the existing tree

`plan.md §4.2` proposed a new `GHC.Platform.Host` module carrying both host
*identity* and *operations*. While standing this up, the tree revealed that
**`GHC.Platform.Host` already exists**: it is an autogenerated module in
`ghc-boot` (produced by Hadrian's `generatePlatformHostHs`) that provides the
host *identity* only — `hostPlatformArch`, `hostPlatformOS`, and
`hostPlatformArchOS :: ArchOS`. It is re-exported by the `ghc` library.

That is exactly the `hostArchOS` half of the plan, already done. So Phase 1 adds
only the **operations** layer, under the same namespace, without disturbing the
generated identity module:

| Role | Module | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Host identity (arch/OS) | `GHC.Platform.Host` | generated in `ghc-boot` (unchanged) |
| Host operations interface | `GHC.Platform.Host.Ops` | new, `compiler/` |
| POSIX implementation | `GHC.Platform.Host.Posix` | new, `compiler/` |
| Windows implementation | `GHC.Platform.Host.Windows` | new, `compiler/` |

Host machine-model facts (word size; `plan.md §4.2`) are deferred to a later
phase and are not part of this layer yet.

## What was added

- **`GHC.Platform.Host.Ops`** — the typed interface: a `HostOps` record (a
  *value*, mirroring how the target `GHC.Platform.Platform` is threaded) plus
  `theHostOps :: HostOps`, a top-level CAF for the platform this `ghc` was built
  for. This module is also the **single OS-selection seam** (`plan.md §4.4`
  option 1): one `#if defined(mingw32_HOST_OS)` chooses which implementation to
  import. It is inside the abstraction layer, so the Phase 0 linter
  (`check-host-cpp.py`) exempts it by design.
- **`GHC.Platform.Host.Posix` / `.Windows`** — implementations populated by
  moving today's host branches *verbatim*. The cabal selects exactly one via an
  `if os(windows)` `other-modules` block, so only the matching implementation is
  compiled.

The initial `HostOps` has one field, `hostGetProcessID`, taken from the
canonical worked example (`plan.md §5`, the `_getpid`/`c_getpid` split in
`GHC.Utils.TmpFs`). It proves the whole seam end to end — interface, both
implementations, OS selection, cabal wiring — while keeping Phase 1 a pure
addition.

## Behaviour preservation

Nothing in the compiler calls `theHostOps` yet, and `GHC.Utils.TmpFs` is
unchanged, so there is no functional change. The duplication between
`TmpFs.getProcessID` and `Host.{Posix,Windows}.getProcessID` is intentional and
temporary: Phase 2 converts the call site to `hostGetProcessID theHostOps` and
deletes the inline `#ifdef`, at which point `TmpFs` leaves the linter allowlist.

## Next (Phase 2)

Convert host call sites file by file (TmpFs → Ar → Panic → Terminal → …), adding
the corresponding `HostOps` field for each, and remove each file from the
`check-host-cpp.py` allowlist as it is cleaned. See the inventory in
`phase0-cpp-classification.md §3`.
